newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia postpones satellite launch as booster fails.
newsitem.headline: Russia postpones satellite launch as booster fails.

text.p: Russia postponed the launch of a new telecommunications satellite on Wednesday due to a booster rocket fault, a space official said.

A spokesman for the Military Space Forces' headquarters told Reuters that the launch was postponed for 24 hours until Thursday after ground specialists detected a problem in the Proton-K rocket at the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
The spokesman did not say what kind of fault was found, but he said a pre-launch team would replace a defective part. "The launch is scheduled for Thursday at 9.46 p.m (0546 GMT)," he added.
The satellite named Express satellite will provide long-range telephone communications and transmit radio and television programmes around Russia.
Russia plans to launch several Express satellites over the next few months to replace 12 outdated Gorizont satellites which have been providing television coverage for Russia.
Earlier this month a Proton booster successfully launched a U.S.-built satellite for the international telecommunications organisation Inmarsat.
